rows.text: The release of 28 September 2001 says that at 4 p.m. that day ('I he taimi 4 efiafi 'o e 'aho ni') Tevita Poasi Tupou resigned ('na'e fakafisi') as Deputy Prime Minister ('Tokoni Palemia'), Attorney General and Minister of Justice, and that the Princess Regent, Pilinisesi Salote Mafile'o Pilolevu Tuita, accepted the request ('Na'e tali 'a e poaki ni').
rows.uncertainty: The resignation and its acceptance are stated for the same day, 28 September 2001, and give the holder's until. The Princess Regent's act is recorded as printed; no regency is observed here. The resignation letter itself was not seen.

rows.text: The same release, on Tevita Poasi Tupou, says that he was appointed Deputy Prime Minister in January 2001 ('i Sanuali 2001 ... ko e 'Eiki Tokoni Palemia') and held that office for nine months ('i he mahina 'e 9').
rows.uncertainty: Retrospective and month only; consistent with the stated effective day of 24 January 2001 (to_dpm_tupou_appointment_effective_20010124) but never itself a holder date. 'toe' (again) is read as part of the sentence's list of successive appointments, not as a second deputy premiership.

rows.text: After the Princess Regent accepted the resignation, she appointed the Minister of Police, Hon. Clive Edwards, Acting Deputy Prime Minister ('na'a ne fakanofo ai 'a e 'Eiki Minisita Polisi, Hon. Clive Edwards, ko e 'Eiki Tokoni Palemia Le'ole'o'), a duty given to him 'i he 'aho ni' (today).
rows.uncertainty: Acting Deputy Prime Minister service: a claim on to_deputy_pm only, never a holder and never a boundary of the substantive office. The end of the acting appointment is not stated.
